name: Marq (The Marq)
headline: Commonwealth Development Corporation of America plans 40 new-construction family apartments (1, 2 and 3 bedrooms, 30% to 60% AMI) at 251 E North Avenue in Trinidad, and won 2025 Round One federal 9% and state credits from CHFA.
why_it_matters: It is a rural deal that got through on its second try: after a 2024 loss the sponsor added six one-bedroom units, 45L credits and a services agreement, and it leans on the Trinidad Housing Authority as special limited partner for a property tax exemption and eight project-based vouchers.

status.label: Credits awarded; sponsor reports financing closed December 2025; construction start not confirmed
status.detail: CHFA listed the award in its 2025 Round One report (as of 2025-05-08). Commonwealth's news page says it celebrated the closing of The Marq in mid-December 2025. No dated public record of a building permit, groundbreaking or vertical construction was found; the application planned a 14-month build with placement in service in April 2027.

next_step: Watch for a City of Trinidad building permit or groundbreaking notice for 251 E North Avenue and a lease-up listing; the application targeted placement in service in April 2027.

key_numbers.meaning: 6 one-bedroom, 17 two-bedroom and 17 three-bedroom units for households at 30%, 50% and 60% AMI.
About $16M over the 10-year credit period, plus $650,000 in state credit.
The applicant's figure, about $463,000 per unit (inferred); cost rose about $3M from the 2024 application after adding units and refining plans.
From the Trinidad Housing Authority, which also joins as special limited partner so the property is tax-exempt.

facts.value: N, I/F: new construction, individuals and families
Vacant 3.1-acre site zoned High Density Residential (up to 25 units per acre); the 2024 application says the site was rezoned from medium to high density and lies in a 2024 Qualified Census Tract
Two 2-story walk-up residential buildings plus a standalone clubhouse, 45,472 gross square feet, timber frame on slab
All-electric, pursuing LEED v4.1 Silver; EV-ready parking
The applicant commits to a 40-year Land Use Restrictive Agreement
Market study by Prior & Associates: overall capture rate 15.5%; lease-up about 8 units a month (full in 5 months). Only one other LIHTC property, Trinidad Artspace Lofts, is in the area

money.note: Awarded in 2025 Round One; $1,600,000 was requested in the February 2025 application.

money.note: About $75,000 in waived tap and permit fees plus a $50,000 cash match, per the applicant.

background.text: The deal first applied in 2024 Round One as a 34-unit project (17 two-bedroom, 17 three-bedroom) requesting $1,350,000 in federal 9% credit, with $850,000 of Division of Housing soft funds in the plan. It was not on the 2025 award list until the resubmission (the 2024 loss is inferred from the resubmission).

In response to CHFA's feedback the sponsor added six one-bedroom units, found 45L credits, signed a services MOU and took design to 30% so the contractor could firm up costs. The December 2024 letter of intent still showed 34 units; the February 2025 application showed 40.

The Division of Housing soft loan in the 2024 plan does not appear in the 2025 source list, which names 9% and state credits, 45L credits, a CHFA permanent loan, deferred developer fee and city Housing Now funds.

Trinidad created the Housing Now program after a 2022 housing needs assessment found 45% of renters cost burdened. The city page describes a $1.5M appropriation and a utility and tap fee deferral incentive for deed-restricted affordable projects, awarded at building permit.

The applicant says the city approved the preliminary site plan and agreed to expedite plan and permit review. It targeted a building permit by December 2025, a February 2026 construction closing and placement in service in April 2027.
Estimated construction cost was $12,737,911 including bonds, insurance, overhead and escalation, with a 5% contingency on top.

Letters of support came from the City of Trinidad, the Trinidad Housing Authority, the South Central Council of Governments, the Trinidad Urban Renewal Authority, the Trinidad & Las Animas County Chamber of Commerce and Las Animas County Health and Human Services. The applicant reports no opposition.
A June 2025 report on a Trinidad City Council work session said construction was expected to break ground by late 2025.
Commonwealth's news page says it celebrated two closings in mid-December 2025, Maplewood Village (Tulsa) and The Marq.

discrepancies.text: CHFA lists the state credit award as $650,000, while The World Journal reported $680,000 in state credits.
The city's Housing Now page describes a $1.5 million appropriation, while the application and The World Journal describe a $2 million city housing commitment.
The application planned a February 2026 construction closing, while Commonwealth reports the closing took place in mid-December 2025.

open_questions: Whether construction has started: no dated building permit, groundbreaking or progress report was found.
Equity investor, credit price, CHFA permanent loan amount and construction lender.
Land seller and purchase price; the application refers to working with the property owner but gives no terms.
Rents, and the date and resolution number of the rezoning to High Density Residential and of the city's Housing Now funding agreement.
No public site plan or rendering was found in a city packet.
